llm.summary: The skill is a coherent workout summarizer, but its exercise-matching helper has overbroad network and caching behavior that should be reviewed before installation.

dimensions.detail: Cloud transcription and dataset lookup are purpose-aligned, but scripts/match_exercises.py accepts an arbitrary --dataset-url, fetches it with urllib, and reads the whole response without host allowlisting, size limits, or integrity checks.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No install hooks, dependency installation, services, scheduled tasks, or package-manager side effects were found in the inspected artifacts.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The workflow is mostly scoped to user-requested summarization, local-by-default handling, and optional transcription backends, but the main skill under-emphasizes that the matching helper may download and cache third-party exercise data.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The helper writes a persistent cache under the user's home directory when no dataset is present; no privilege escalation or background persistence was found, but the cache is populated automatically and can retain mutable remote data.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose, workflow, and helper scripts fit strength-training transcript/audio summarization, duration calculation, and exercise-name matching; no deceptive role changes or unrelated capabilities were found.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing if you require offline-only behavior or tight network controls. Prefer using an existing transcript or local Whisper, provide a local pinned dataset with --dataset, avoid untrusted --dataset-url values, and be aware that Groq/OpenAI transcription sends audio to the selected provider.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: Exercise dataset matching is purpose-aligned and documented in the workflow, so the broad mismatch claim is downgraded; the remaining issue is under-disclosed automatic remote fetch/cache behavior.
[TM1] expected: The Groq curl example is a normal transcription API call using an environment API key, not evidence of command abuse by itself.
[LP3] expected: File access, shell helpers, and optional network transcription are expected for this skill, but explicit permission scoping would make the authority clearer.
[E1] expected: Audio upload to Groq is expected only when a cloud transcription backend is selected and credentials are configured; users should understand that audio leaves the local machine in that mode.
[SDI-2] expected: Outbound HTTP for the exercise dataset supports canonical exercise matching, but it is not prominent in the main skill instructions.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Using a mutable GitHub main-branch JSON without a pinned version, digest, or schema validation is avoidable and expands the trust boundary beyond what the core summary task requires.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The persistent cache write is useful for performance, but automatic first-run download and cache creation lacks a clear user notice or opt-in.
[T09] unexpected: Allowing arbitrary dataset URLs is broader than needed for this purpose and creates SSRF/resource-consumption risk if arguments are influenced.
[T08] unexpected: A third-party dataset is expected for matching, but relying on mutable, unverified remote content is not necessary for the stated workflow.
